ART MORA Gallery is pleased to present “Dear Bunny,” the second solo exhibition by Sun Kim. Following his participation in the ART MORA Residency Program and his first solo exhibition in 2018, Kim returns to the gallery eight years later with a new body of work.

The rabbit that appears throughout Kim’s work is a reflection of the artist himself. Through this recurring figure, he explores dreams, family, everyday happiness, and the thoughts and emotions that sometimes become tangled within us. His rabbits are both dreamers and embodiments of the dreams he creates.

Kim’s sculptural practice has evolved from wood carving to resin and, more recently, 3D printing. This exhibition primarily features his recent 3D-printed works, along with a large-scale rabbit and two cat sculptures hand-carved from foam board at the gallery. While his materials and methods continue to change, one desire remains at the heart of his work: to keep dreaming happy dreams.

Life does not always allow us to hold on to those dreams. We experience hurt, uncertainty, and moments when we forget how to dream. Yet Kim continues to give his dreams and emotions physical form, hoping they may offer others warmth and the strength to begin again. “Dear Bunny,” is a tender letter from the artist to himself—a gesture of comfort to the self that has traveled through life, and a wish to continue dreaming of happiness.

metadata.description: Founded in 2017, 1202 Contemporary, formerly Gallery 1202, is a cornerstone art institution located in the South Bay of the San Francisco Bay Area. 1202 Contemporary has brought high-quality exhibitions to the area for the past 8 years, shown at art fairs across the United States, and assisted in placing works in museum and private collections across the globe. The gallery was originally opened in the historic Pixley house in downtown Gilroy and continues to serve Gilroy and the surrounding areas in it's new location within The Clove Art Complex. The new location is set inside the historic Milias building, dating back to the 1920s. In 2022, 1202 Contemporary transitioned to a 501(c)3 organization in order to further support artists in their career, and to bring contemporary art into Gilroy, Morgan Hill, Hollister, and surrounding areas. The gallery's mission is to be an inclusive, welcoming space for the community while focusing on promoting marginalized artists. We strive to amplify the silenced voices in the art-world, including womxn, and BIPOC artists, artists with young families, and artists who deal in alternative mediums, and subject-matter.

#### **Base Camp Studios** “BCS” is a creative community rooted in the heart of Belltown, Seattle. Located in two long-vacant buildings, **BCS** offers studio space to a wide range of artists, designers, and makers, along with two galleries that regularly feature exhibitions, installations, and collaborative events.

#### **Our mission** is to provide inclusive, affordable, and inspiring spaces where Seattle-based creatives can work, connect, and grow in community. By fostering collaboration and visibility, **BCS** aims to help revitalize the downtown core with creativity and strengthen the city’s wider arts ecosystem—making space not just for art, but for community.

# On View Now

Featured

[Sarah Barnett: Spectacle of Being](https://gallery110.com/exhibitions/sarah-barnett-spectacle-of-being)

[Sarah Barnett: Spectacle of Being](https://gallery110.com/exhibitions/sarah-barnett-spectacle-of-being)

Drawing from medical imagery and emerging technologies, these paintings present the operating theater as a site where the vulnerable human body, apparatus, machine, image and observer converge. They reflect on the strange reality unfolding as once-imagined technologies become increasingly intimate with our lives.

[Read more →](https://gallery110.com/exhibitions/sarah-barnett-spectacle-of-being)

[Matthew Behrend: Radiant Echoes](https://gallery110.com/exhibitions/matthew-behrend-radiant-echoes)

[Matthew Behrend: Radiant Echoes](https://gallery110.com/exhibitions/matthew-behrend-radiant-echoes)

Light settles into metal the way a dream lingers after waking. These patina works mark the signs of arriving somewhere inward: ease, recognition, elements falling into place. Some sounds are heard only after they pass. Come and listen for what returns.

[Read more →](https://gallery110.com/exhibitions/matthew-behrend-radiant-echoes)

[Marcus Lelle: Reclaimed : Renewed](https://gallery110.com/exhibitions/marcus-lelle-reclaimed-renewed)

[Marcus Lelle: Reclaimed : Renewed](https://gallery110.com/exhibitions/marcus-lelle-reclaimed-renewed)

Reclaimed : Renewed explores the relationship between art and artist. By using recycled materials the art becomes sustainable, and incorporating images into wearable pieces, the artist aims to share the tactile experience of creating. This exhibition is comprised of a variety of techniques that show the range of the Cyanotype process.

[Read more →](https://gallery110.com/exhibitions/marcus-lelle-reclaimed-renewed)

metadata.description: Cindy Lisica Gallery (and sister-company, Art Fox Travel) currently operates out of the San Francisco Bay Area at Magnolia Court in Oakland, as well as guest-curated shows and the best art fairs across the US. The gallery was originally founded in 2014 as Revision Space in Pittsburgh's Art & Design Zone, followed by a second location in 2016 as Cindy Lisica Gallery at 4411 Montrose in Houston's Museum District, quickly becoming known for exhibiting both emerging artists and established art stars by placing their work into impressive shows, catalogs, collections and museums. Owner Dr. Cindy Lisica (PhD, Art History) is a curator, art tour guide, writer, dealer, consultant, and professor with active connections around the world, representing the contemporary art world through exhibitions, public talks, small VIP group itineraries and events. Check it all out at cindylisicagallery.com, IG: @cindylisicagallery and artfoxtravel.com, IG: @artfoxtravel

## _Rococo Puffs_ 
Tess Michalik

Nov 6th–Nov 28th, 2026

_Rococo Puffs_ 
Tess Michalik

Opening Reception: Friday, November 6th, 5–8 PM 
Exhibition Dates: November 6th-28th, 2026

“_Rococo Puffs_ is a show of fantastical floral spaces. Landscapes, design motifs, and floral arrangements in all states of bloom; a memento mori, peak blossom as the zenith of a flower’s short-lived existence. They also reference European textile design of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. They borrow the meandering curves and vines of brocaded silks and woven tapestries.

They are made with oil paints, brushes, and palette knives on canvases or panels. Their surface is thick impasto paint that has been put down on the canvas wet into wet, thickly and heavily, twisting and pulling, scraping and burying, and reapplying paint to the substrate. The working process can be sculptural in applying the paint, recording motion with gestures preserved in the marking of the paint.”

Please join Gallery Century at the Seattle Art Fair, the Pacific Northwest's premier contemporary and modern art fair (July 23rd-26th at Lumen Field).

To preview the show : [Go Here](https://www.gallerycentury.com/events-1/seattle-art-fair-2026)

Passes are good for the duration of the fair, including the Opening Night Party from 6-9:00pm on Thursday, July 23rd.

---

# Our Vision

Art elevates the human spirit in a way that nothing else does. It changes people's lives, one experience at a time.

Gallery Century offers quality examples by important American, European, Asian and Indigenous artists from the mid 20th century to the present and our diverse inventory includes more than 800 artworks.

We showcase many legendary figures of the art world as well as more contemporary artists whose beautiful and emotionally expressive works bring joy and meaning into the lives of discerning collectors worldwide.

We also feature artists who are overlooked, undervalued and haven't achieved the celebrity status of some of their contemporaries but who nevertheless painted superior works.

The gallery has placed works of art in major public, private, and corporate collections

Our extensive knowledge of the art world spans a wide range of artists and media, allowing us to offer art advisory and curatorial services to all levels of private and corporate collections

[$0.00 0 Cart](https://fotovatatelier.com/#)

Now in its third generation, with almost 85 years of experience, Fotovat family has been engaged in the creation and trading of Persian miniature paintings since 1940. The accomplished masters at Fotovat Atelier currently create exquisite artworks under the expert supervision of Master Mostafa Fotovat.

Mostafa Fotovat is an award-winning artist and gallerist born in Persia whose entire life has been dedicated to creating, teaching and promoting Persian miniature and his artworks have been exhibited in many countries in Europe and in the United States. He learned the art from his father in the early years and developed his skills by attending courses from major masters of the time. He is currently engaged in collaborations with prestigious museums and discerning private collectors, creating exclusive pieces of illuminated manuscripts and restoring  antique museum artifacts.

Miniature painting is a term applied both to Western portrait miniatures and to the Persian, Indian and Otoman forms of manuscript painting. The origins of the term “Miniature” has nothing to do with the size although a miniature painting can be as small as the surface of a finger nail or as big as a wall panel. The name is derived from the “minium”, or red lead, used by the medieval illuminators.

Persian miniature painting represent a tradition that was continued into modern times with the most important function of book illustration. It gave a visual image to the literary plot, making it more enjoyable, and easier to understand. Miniature developed into a marriage of artistic and poetic languages and obtained a deep and sincere accordance with poetry. The subjects of early Persian miniatures included religious and historical narrative, cosmic maps, and medical, palmistry, and astrological charts, as well as illustrations to poems, songs, and romantic epics. These were generally painted in gouache on paper, with occasional gold- or silver-leaf embellishment. The linear design was first drawn with a brush in delicate contours and soft shading. Landscape and architectural detail was as well observed as in that of the principal figures.

The contemporary Persian miniature is distinctive in that it goes against the common conception of an Avant-garde. Its practitioners innovate not by rejecting what went before them but through mastering traditional skills and then moving beyond them.

The significance of craft skills makes miniature painting stand out from the other techniques of painting and since attention to the detail is very important, creating a miniature painting can be a painstaking effort with a narrow margin of error.

- Fri, May 8, 2026 5:00 PM Wed, Jul 8, 2026 5:00 PM
- Gallery Mack [(map)](http://maps.google.com?q=2100 Western Avenue Seattle, WA, 98121 United States)

We are pleased to announce ROOTED, Sherrie Newman’s second solo exhibition at Gallery Mack.

Following the success of her 2025 show, HOME, Newman continues to explore themes of belonging and the deep connections found within home, landscape, and place. This new exhibition features her signature heavily textured acrylic and mixed media paintings alongside a return to charcoal drawing. By incorporating trees and expansive landscapes, she further develops her visual language surrounding these themes.

Sherrie Newman is originally from Western New York state, earned her BFA in Drawing and Painting from Alfred University, and has resided in Seattle for 25 years.

#### LINDA JO NAZARENUS - [_Distant Visions_](https://www.harrisharveygallery.com/linda-jo-nazarenus-distantvisions)

November 5 - 28, 2026 
Artist Reception: First Thursday, November 5, 6-8 PM 
Artist in Attendance

Linda Jo Nazarenus creates richly detailed paintings of expansive landscapes and the wildlife that inhabits them. Influenced by the Northern European masters of the Renaissance, she builds her images through layers of thin oil glazes, rendering fur, stone, foliage, and atmospheric light with remarkable precision. Drawing on the landscapes of Sweden and the American Southwest, her work expresses both reverence for nature and a fascination with its mystery.

In _Distant Visions_, animals and landscapes are interwoven with human symbols of longing, memory, belief, and our desire to reach beyond the known. The Very Large Array’s dishes turn toward outer space; an obelisk marks the Trinity Site; a solitary church, a sacred tree near Pueblo ruins, a “lucky” keepsake of a lost loved one, and Seattle’s Space Needle become charged with personal and mystical associations. Juxtaposed with animals and the natural world, these objects and places take on an uncanny, otherworldly presence. Nazarenus gives her animals an unusual sense of awareness, making them seem as conscious of the viewer as they are of their own precarious existence. Her landscapes similarly resist being merely scenic, becoming spaces of uncertainty, contemplation, and wonder.

---

Upcoming Exhibition

#### _COLLECTED_ 
A Holiday Group Exhibition

December 3, 2026 - January 30, 2027 
Artists’ Reception: First Thursday, December 3, 6-8 PM

Bringing together recent work and collectables by more than 30 artists from across the Northwest and West Coast, this Holiday group exhibition offers a multifaceted look at the region’s contemporary creative landscape. Moving fluidly between painting, photography, printmaking, sculpture, and mixed media, the exhibition embraces a wide range of perspectives, materials, and artistic languages.

Many of the works emerged from periods of quiet observation, introspection, and change, revealing artists responding to both personal and broader cultural shifts. The result is a compelling collection that reflects the richness and diversity of practices shaping contemporary art on the West Coast.

United by a shared spirit of curiosity and experimentation, these works speak to themes of transformation, resilience, and renewal. Together, they create an expansive and engaging portrait of artists continually redefining their practices and the possibilities of contemporary expression.

Previous Exhibition

#### HART JAMES - [_Poems of the Earth_](https://www.harrisharveygallery.com/hartjames-poemsofthearth) 
& 
GREGG LAANANEN - [_Fire in the Moon_](https://www.harrisharveygallery.com/gregg-laananen-fire-in-the-moon)

October 1 - 31, 2026 
Artists’ Reception: First Thursday, October 1, 6-8 PM

Pacific Northwest artist Hart James channels elemental forces into bold abstractions. The artist explores the inherent connection between the individual and their natural environment. Her compositions rendered in oil and charcoal, evoke the movement of water, the whisper of air, and the enduring weight of stone. With a deep knowledge of the Northwest Mystics, she paints in an abstract manner to carry this tradition forward to the present. James’s work speaks of the energy of nature—every painting is an attempt to reunite with an existence symbiotic with the natural world. 

Gregg Laananen is a self-taught artist living and working in the Skagit Valley. His artwork is informed by observations made from nature, automatic drawing, the role of chance and intuition, material investigation, as well as the interplay of different kinds of abstraction. Alternating between painting in the studio and out of doors, Gregg Laananen breathes life and color into the Pacific Northwest landscape with his visceral interpretations of water falls, forests, and isolated elements of nature. Plants, flowers and flumes are rendered with visceral, highly textured paint application in a style that values simplicity and immediacy. The artist also creates enchanting floral still life scenes. Lannanen’s surroundings and their emotional effect on him determine his approach, which can be described as neo-expressionist.

# Fantagraphics Bookstore & Gallery

**Fantagraphics Bookstore & Gallery** 
1201 South Vale Street (at Airport Way S.) 
Seattle, WA 98108 
Mon. – Sat 11:30 – 8 
Sun 11:30 – 5 
Call for holiday hours 
206-557-4910

If you live in or plan to visit the great Pacific Northwest, be sure to visit our very own storefront, simply called the **Fantagraphics Bookstore & Gallery**, in the happenin’ Seattle neighborhood of Georgetown. The culmination of a years-long dream, the store opened in October 2006, with a grand opening celebration held on December 2 of that year (and swinging anniversary parties each year thereafter). The store contains everything Fantagraphics has in print (as well as our adult imprint Eros Comix), including **exclusive merchandise**, plus a selection of the best alternative comics from our fellow publshers and other surprises! It also houses our hallowed **Damaged Room**, featuring heavily discounted and often out-of-print books unavailable anywhere else. (And vinyl junkies be warned: the Bookstore shares space with [Georgetown Records](http://www.georgetownrecords.net/), a Seattle record-collectors’ mecca. And it is just a short stroll from some of Seattle’s best and most beloved coffee shops, taverns, eateries and art spaces.) The space also has room for art exhibitions, with a new exhibit mounted about once a month. We also host readings, screenings, music and other performances.

#### About LIC Gallery

### Contemporary Art on Seattle’s Waterfront

[Learn More About LIC Gallery](https://lostincomposition.com/about/)

**Located on Seattle’s waterfront, LIC Gallery presents a curated collection of contemporary art from exceptional emerging and established artists.**

**From bold statement pieces to intimate works for personal spaces, we help collectors and the art-curious discover artwork that reflects their tastes, enriches their environments, and leaves lasting impressions.**

**Come find something that takes your breath away.**

## Gallery updates

### [Leeah Joo](https://lostincomposition.com/leeah-joo-draped/)

Leeah Joo’s show _Draped_ has just had the curtain pulled back. Oops, Parrhasius already tried that with Zeuxis! Her show opens on November 4, 2026, and runs until November 29, 2026.

### [Elise Wagner](https://lostincomposition.com/elise-wagner-intersections/)

Elise Wagner’s _Intersections_ opens on November 4, 2026, and runs through November 29, 2026. This show explores navigation: how we locate ourselves, interpret patterns, and find our way through change.

### [Donna Bates](https://lostincomposition.com/donna_bates_solo_show/)

## Getting here

LIC Gallery is located in the Maritime Building on Seattle’s waterfront, directly across the street from the Washington State Ferry terminal and next door to Sub Pop Records. We’re steps from Pike Place Market, the Seattle Aquarium, and Overlook Walk. Street parking is available on Alaskan Way, and the Madison Street Garage and Western Avenue Garage are both within easy walking distance. If you’re waiting for a ferry, come get lost in the art.

## _Meow Brow 2026_

The cat came back: it’s the return of Meow Brow at Gallery ERGO! Dozens of our favorite artists doing their thing on fun little birch panels shaped like cat heads, with 10% of all sales going to a local animal shelter. This annual show has been a favorite for years, and the work in this year’s edition is really great! 

Opening reception to be held at our gallery in Seattle on Friday, November 13th from 5-8pm. No RSVP necessary. Work also now available online!

[Explore the Show](https://www.galleryergo.com/shop/meow-brow-2026/C3ZZCRQ6ZMEZARPEQIITGIFD)

## Mike Egan: _In Death’s Garden_

Gallery ERGO is very proud to welcome Youngstown, Ohio-based Artist Mike Egan for a brand new solo show in his bold and iconically funereal style. We can’t wait to share this one with you! 

We'll have an opening reception at our gallery located in Seattle's historic Pike Place Market on Friday, Oct 9th from 5-8pm. No RSVP necessary. A collector’s preview will be available by request.

[Opening Oct 9th](https://www.galleryergo.com/shop/mike-egan-in-deaths-garden/RZHJQBYJAOT6NH6A5SJY2JBO)

## Casey Weldon: _Endless Bummer_

Gallery ERGO is stoked to present a fresh new show from our friend Casey Weldon! Casey’s surreal and imaginative work has been a favorite for years at ERGO, and we couldn’t be more hyped to host the artist for their debut solo show with us. 

We’ll have an opening reception at our gallery located inside Seattle’s historic Pike Place Market on October 9th, from 5-8pm. The artist will be in attendance. No RSVP necessary. Collector’s previews will be available by request and for those on our Previews list.

[Opening Oct 9th](https://www.galleryergo.com/shop/casey-weldon-endless-bummer/2QI4MXFIKZ2Y2NHEGF3BTXO2)

## Yi Du: _An Antidote Lost and Found_

Seattle artist Yi Du has been a regular contributor to our group shows for the last couple years, consistently submitting fantastic work each time. We now have the honor of hosting her debut solo show, and Yi has made a truly beautiful body of new works for us! 

Opening reception to be held at our gallery located in Seattle's historic Pike Place Market on Friday, Oct 9th from 5-8pm. No RSVP necessary. A collector’s preview will be available by request.

[Opening Oct 9th](https://www.galleryergo.com/shop/yi-du-an-antidote-lost-and-found/O5VBHREMYC3UCDCBVNGWOR3W)

## Gallery ERGO 5 Year Anniversary

They say time flies when you’re having fun, and we’re certainly having fun at Gallery ERGO. Hard to believe five years have already passed since we opened our doors! That’s five years of shows, five years of working with some of the very coolest artists doing it today, five years of wonderful collectors supporting living artists and adding incredible works to their collections. 

In commemoration, we’re holding a big 5-year Anniversary Show at ERGO, and we’ve gathered fantastic new work from 40+ of our friends to celebrate. The opening reception will be held on Friday, Sep 11th from 5-8pm, no RSVP necessary.

[Explore the Show](https://www.galleryergo.com/shop/ergo-5-year-anniversary/IIEBBJRAHIQKBAH7Y52P3O7W)

## SNYDER: _Chromatic Wilderness_

We’re proud to present a solo show from Berlin-based visual artist SNYDER. Known for his work at both mural and canvas scale, SNYDER has shown with us for several years now and always sends us the coolest work. We are really excited to share a full body of work this time, and he has cooked up some fantastic pieces for us! 

Opening Friday, Sep 11th 5-8pm. No RSVP necessary.

[Explore the Show](https://www.galleryergo.com/shop/snyder-chromatic-wilderness/JYJLD5CKVY3HS53RHF3YNDEB)

Check out our wide selection of incredible original works, including original paintings, sculptures, and more.

The John Natsoulas Gallery is pleased to host the solo exhibition of renown sculptor Kensuke Yamada. Showcased in the first floor gallery, this exhibition will include a collection of the newest ceramic sculptures by the artist. His distinctive style and unique subjects have made him one of the most notable voices in the contemporary art world today.

[Learn more!](https://natsoulas.com/currentexhibitions/kensuke-yamada-october-28-november-28-2026)

The John Natsoulas Gallery is thrilled to be hosting the solo exhibition of Rene Martucci’s ceramic sculptures from October 28 to November 28, titled “Balance and Perspective.” René Martucci (b. 1960) received a bachelor of arts degree from the University of California, Davis where she studied with Robert Arneson, Manual Neri and Wayne Thiebaud. Working under the rigorous and inspirational guidance of Robert Arneson, Martucci developed impressive craftsmanship and a desire to explore and challenge herself as an artist.

[Learn more!](https://natsoulas.com/currentexhibitions/rene-martucci-balance-and-perspective-october-28-november-28-2026)

First Thursday Art Walk, November 5, 5-8 

Second Saturday Artist Reception December 12, 2-4 

​Join us for an exhilarating art show at LYNN HANSON GALLERY, where we proudly present the works of three talented artists. Each artist brings a unique perspective that blends realism with contemporary themes, inviting viewers to engage with thought-provoking subject matter. Mark your calendars for this special opening, as it’s an opportunity to support our local artists. Don’t miss out on the chance to experience the warmth and inspiration that LYNN HANSON GALLERY has to offer!

Email(Required) Submit [Instagram Logo](https://www.instagram.com/pghglasscenter/) [Facebook Logo](https://www.facebook.com/pghglasscenter) [Youtube Logo](https://www.youtube.com/@pghglasscenter) All content © Pittsburgh Glass Center 2026 | [ADA Notice](https://www.pittsburghglasscenter.org/accessibility/) | [Privacy](https://www.pittsburghglasscenter.org/privacy-policy/) [Policy](https://www.pittsburghglasscenter.org/privacy-policy/) [Achieve logo](https://achievecauses.com/) | | ##### Hot Shop Activities
With the help of an instructor, participants will learn how to transform 2,000°F molten glass into a unique glass artwork. Sculpted items will be manipulated and shaped with various metal hand tools. Blown items will be inflated via a flexible tube attached to a blow pipe. The Hot Shop, as the name might suggest, can get warm at times, particularly during summer months. That being said, the activity will only take about 10-15 minutes per person so you won’t be warm for long. We encourage our guests to wear lighter, natural material clothing for safety and comfort. Visitors are welcome to bring water bottles and a water fountain/filling station is available. These activities will involves sitting, standing, and walking around. Suitable for ages 5 and up. | | --- | --- | | | ##### Kiln Shop Fusing Activities
Combine brilliantly colored pieces of glass granules and thin glass strands to create a one-of-a-kind luminous fused glass artwork. Once you design it, we’ll fire it, so that all pieces become one. Participants will work seated in our climate-controlled Classroom and with room temperature pieces of glass. You will begin with a glass tile that acts as your “canvas,” then arrange the colorful glass granules and thin glass strands into a design of your choosing. Once the designs are complete, suncatchers are placed in a kiln overnight to melt (fuse) together forever. Suitable for ages 5 and up. | | | ##### Flame Shop Activities
With the help of an instructor, participants will learn how to use tools and a tabletop torch to melt and manipulate glass rods and transform them into truly one-of-a-kind objects. These activities take place in our climate controlled Flame Shop, which involves working with a flame, but is not nearly as warm as our Hot Shop. Participants will be sitting at a workstation, making this option slightly more accessible and less physically demanding. metadata.title: Pittsburgh Glass Center
metadata.description: Pittsburgh Glass Center (PGC) is a nonprofit, public-access education center; an art gallery; a state-of-the-art glass studio; a community builder; and a hub for innovation and creativity. Anyone can take classes, explore the contemporary glass gallery, and watch the live hot glass demonstrations. World-renowned glass artists come here to create and teach.

# A little more art in your life.

Art to live with. Creativity to make your own.

[Explore the art](https://nino.studio/collections/originals) [Make art with me](https://nino.studio/pages/workshops)

Ways in

## Bring art home, or make your own.

Art has a funny way of making life a little more interesting. Here's everything you can do with me, all in one place.

### Collect

One-of-a-kind paintings, small surprises by mail, and prints for every wall.

[Shop\\ \\ **Original paintings**\\ \\ One-of-a-kind abstracts, made in my Seattle studio.\\ \\ Browse originals](https://nino.studio/collections/originals) [Auction\\ \\ **Nino's Auction House**\\ \\ One original at a time, open for bids. Latest: Art Pocket #005.\\ \\ Visit the auction](https://collect.nino.studio) [Monthly\\ \\ **Art in your mailbox**\\ \\ A signed print or a small original, every month.\\ \\ Join a club](https://nino.studio/collections/collect-subscribe) [Small ways in\\ \\ **Prints & books**\\ \\ Signed prints, sketchbooks and art books.\\ \\ Shop prints](https://nino.studio/collections/print-shop)

Interior designer or art consultant? [Join the trade program](https://nino.studio/pages/trade) for a special rate on original work, or [ask about a commission](https://nino.studio/pages/contact).

### Create

Places to experiment, make a mess, and rediscover the fun of making.

[In person\\ \\ **Workshops & retreats**\\ \\ Small groups in Seattle, across the US and in France.\\ \\ See dates](https://nino.studio/pages/workshops) [Online membership\\ \\ **Spice Art Club**\\ \\ Make art, get feedback, and keep going with other artists.\\ \\ Explore the club](https://nino.studio/pages/spice-art-club) [Start here\\ \\ **Abstract for beginners**\\ \\ New to abstract painting? Begin at your own pace.\\ \\ Begin](https://nino.studio/pages/abstract-for-beginners) [Private events · Seattle\\ \\ **Artcuterie**\\ \\ An all-you-can-create art buffet for your group.\\ \\ Plan a gathering](https://nino.studio/pages/artcuterie)

Collectors, collaborators & press

## Collected by homes, hotels and companies.

“Nino’s beautiful painting is the centerpiece of our dining area and kitchen. It is alive and joyous, and perfectly complements the design of our home.”

Nelle & Matt · Collectors

“I purchased a small snack piece several years ago and am still in love with it. I usually rotate the art I’ve collected, but this small artwork always stays on the wall.”

Paula Weed · Collector

“I feel a lightness and more joy has been brought back into my practice.”

Barbara Helton · Workshop

“I love the encouragement and sharing that takes place in this community. There’s a wonderful sense of playfulness here too!”

Karen Miraldi · Spice Art Club

About Nino

A little less perfect. A little more free. A little more you.

I'm an abstract artist and designer who still loves not knowing exactly what will happen next. I follow a color, a shape or a memory and see where it takes me.

Art isn't just what hangs on our walls. It's how it makes us feel, and the little ways it brings us back to ourselves.

metadata.description: Melissa Morgan Fine Art [MMFA] stands as the premier art gallery destination in Southern California, dedicated to representing cutting-edge national and international contemporary artists and exhibiting a diverse range of 2D, 3D, and new media fine artworks. Nestled on El Paseo Drive in Palm Desert, California, our 6,000-square-foot art gallery, complemented by a half-acre outdoor sculpture garden, serves as a haven for fine art enthusiasts. Each year, MMFA hosts an extensive lineup of solo and group exhibitions, both within the gallery and amidst the serene backdrop of our sculpture garden. Additionally, we actively participate in multiple art fairs across the country, consistently promoting and sharing the world of fine art with a broader audience. Beyond our exhibitions, our art gallery extends its offerings to include private consultations, acquisitions, confidential advisory services, and seamless art installation. We also cater to collectors, corporations, and institutions, providing specialized art storage and transportation solutions, ensuring the safety and preservation of your fine art collection.

#### JULIE ANDERSON MATHIAS

In Studio

OCTOBER 1, 2026 - JANUARY 17, 2027

[EXPLORE NOW](https://www.seimandileprieur.com/exhibition/in-studio)

[​​​​In Studio](https://www.seimandileprieur.com/exhibition/in-studio) brings together twelve paintings by Julie Anderson Mathias, whose work is rooted in her lifelong interest in color and abstraction. Her approach has been shaped by her background in interior architecture and her decades of experience as a muralist, working directly on buildings and at an architectural scale.

​

While studying at Syracuse University in the early 1970s, Mathias encountered the work of Morris Louis and Helen Frankenthaler, whose approaches to color and composition left a lasting impression. Her later career in interior architecture, including at Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, further developed her understanding of scale and proportion.

​

Mathias typically begins her paintings with sketches, color studies, and geometric structures. As the work develops, however, the original plan gives way to a dialogue between intention and discovery. Throughout this process, color remains at the heart of Mathias’s practice.

[Learn more](https://www.seimandileprieur.com/exhibition/in-studio)

# Visit the gallery

SEIMANDI & LEPRIEUR is a contemporary art gallery in the heart of Santa Barbara’s art district, founded by a French couple with a discerning eye for artists of national and international stature. The gallery presents a carefully considered program of exhibitions, changing approximately every two months, with a strong emphasis on aesthetics and thoughtful presentation, creating an environment in which each artist’s work can be experienced at its best and in a setting befitting the quality of their work. The gallery also maintains a collection of works available to collectors, with private viewings available by appointment, and works closely with interior designers to develop tailored art selections and presentation proposals for private residences.

Located near State Street and the Santa Barbara Museum of Art, the gallery offers a serene, light-filled space designed for both contemplation and discovery. With expansive wall space, it is designed for ambitious, curatorially driven exhibitions that give each artist’s work the presence it deserves, inviting visitors to explore new perspectives and discover a work that speaks to them.

​

Through artist talks, exhibition openings, the First Thursday Art Walk, and private events, the gallery offers visitors a direct connection to the contemporary art scene.

### Luminosity – 2026

10/01/2026 - 11/28/2026

#### First Thursday Art Walk: Nov 5, 5-8pm

NOW EXTENDED THROUGH NOVEMBER 28!

Bringing together the rich cultural heritage of Native art and the innovative spirit of the Studio Glass movement, Luminosity celebrates the evolving artistry of Northwest Native Glass. Featured prominently are Preston Singletary (Tlingit), Raven Skyriver (Tlingit), and Dan Friday (Lummi), whose distinctive approaches continue to expand the possibilities of glass as a contemporary Native art form. Their work joins that of other artists drawn to the medium, creating a dynamic showcase of diverse perspectives, inventive techniques, and luminous expression.

Stonington Gallery has long supported the creative exchange between Northwest Coast Indigenous art and contemporary glassmaking. Each year, Luminosity offers a fresh look at this ever-evolving artistic landscape, honoring its roots while celebrating the artists who continue to move it forward.

# Welcome to Stonington Gallery

Stonington Gallery is a Northwest Coast Native art gallery based in Seattle, Washington exhibiting an exceptional collection of contemporary masterworks from the Pacific Northwest and Alaska. Serving Seattle since 1979, the gallery is respected for the depth and quality of its collection, exceptional service, and knowledgeable staff.

For visitors seeking to understand the character of Seattle and the wider region, this contemporary Northwest Coast Native art gallery offers a rich cultural introduction, affirms, and is proof of the vitality of living Indigenous cultures and artists. The gallery presents works across carving, works on paper, glass sculpture, and contemporary media, highlighting both renowned masters and emerging artists.

Our mission is to provide an ideal environment for the presentation, enjoyment, and understanding of premier contemporary Northwest Coast Native art, while fostering deeper appreciation for the artists who create them. This commitment has led the gallery to present exhibitions and installations at museums, convention centers, government buildings, SeaTac Airport, the Seattle Aquarium, international art fairs, and venues abroad, including Nantes, France.

The gallery staff acknowledges that the gallery and larger city of Seattle occupies unceded [Duwamish lands.](https://www.duwamishtribe.org/)

## T H E N C E   B Y  D E S C E N T

## Seattle

About

Photography by Erik Sven

## 01 about

Thence By Descent (TBD) is a Seattle-based design gallery and dealer for collectible furniture, lighting, and objects, specializing in works by American Craft legend George Nakashima and Mira Nakashima. TBD is the Pacific Northwest's only source for authentic, handcrafted Nakashima works. Founded by Mark Tan, Thence By Descent’s mission is to:

Spark an obsessive appreciation for

heirloom-quality design.

Prior to relocating to Seattle in 2017, Mark lived in New York City for 18 years, where space limitations forced him to ruthlessly edit, curate, and prioritize, guided by principles around craft, form, function, quality, materials, and history. The pieces he treasured most were those with interesting provenances — particularly those passed down through generations within a family (“thence by descent” is a term often used by auction houses, museums, galleries, and specialists to describe this particular transfer of ownership).

Thence By Descent advocates a sustainability-forward approach to procurement as a local source and by helping clients acquire heirloom-quality designs intended to be preserved for future generations.

Whether you are an established architectural or design studio, a seasoned collector, or simply wandering with a curious eye, Thence By Descent embraces your interest and is here to help spark an obsessive appreciation for fine design.

Clients

## 05 consultation

Thence By Descent offers personalized consultation services for clients seeking exceptional design pieces by American studio craft woodworkers, George and Mira Nakashima. With a deep understanding of Nakashima’s craftsmanship and design philosophy, we assist in sourcing one-of-a-kind, heirloom-quality furniture that not only meets your aesthetic and functional needs but also your financial investment objectives. Our services include:

Personalized Research and Sourcing: We leverage our expertise and understanding of the network to identify Nakashima pieces that align with your specific needs (and obsessions), whether you are seeking a classic work such as the Conoid chair or a rare masterpiece.

Curated Selection: Drawing from a curated selection of collectible pieces, we offer options that hold both historical interest and enduring value. Each item is chosen for its authenticity, craftsmanship, and potential to appreciate over time.

Value Guidance: Beyond sourcing, we provide advice on the provenance, condition, and market value of each piece, ensuring that your investment aligns with both your lifestyle and financial objectives.

Seamless Procurement Process: Our service ensures a smooth and discreet procurement process, managing every detail from research and brokerage to final delivery and installation as needed, allowing you to focus on enjoying your new purchase.

Thence By Descent’s tailored consultation services are designed to support your next strategic acquisition.

NEW ARTIST

Spectrum Fine Art is pleased to announce the representation of painter Laura Hudson. 

Born and raised on Whidbey Island, WA, Hudson, has a deep connection to the Pacific Northwest. Her work stems from lived experience, memory, and a curiosity about the relationship between humanity and the natural world. She is drawn to moments where human and creature meet in a fragile, respectful balance - moments that hold space for both uncertainty and hope. Influenced by Katherine Bradford and Milton Avery, along with years of experimentation, Hudson has uncovered a way of painting that feels both intuitive and newly discovered.

metadata.title: Home | Spectrum Fine Art
metadata.description: Spectrum Fine Art is a contemporary art gallery in the heart of the Madrona neighborhood of Seattle. Founded in 2023 by Leah Steen and Jessica Cantlin, Spectrum Fine Art represents emerging and mid-career artists across all mediums. Originally from Nashville, Leah is a successful interior designer who routinely curates artwork for her clients’ residences. Jessica, a Seattle native, is a fine art photographer who has been selling and showcasing her work in the Pacific Northwest and abroad since recovering from her law practice in 2012. Together, Jessica and Leah have united to create a space connecting artists previously unrepresented in the Seattle art market with Pacific Northwest collectors. Spectrum aims to showcase art that is fresh, joyful, colorful, perhaps a little left of center — never dull.

# Since 1961

Sixty-five years have passed. It is simply hard to believe in May of 1961, Gordon Woodside rented a large old home on First Hill, built art walls and painted the modest building. We printed a few hundred flyers and made a list of all the people we knew who could afford to spend a few hundred dollars.  Not a very long list! And opened a fine art gallery dedicated to the artists of our region.

So much has changed since then.  We have been through thirteen Presidents, the end of the Cold war and the dawn of the information age.  We have seen the hyper-revolution of the technology age and it’s effect on nearly every aspect of our lives.

Throughout all of this growth and change, the allure of art has remained.  People collect art for many reasons. They wish to display art on the walls of their home or business, however the desire to collect art runs far deeper than that.  There seems to be a need to connect with the unique, the handmade and to journey to a place where original ideas, craft and beauty are necessary to subordinate speed and quantity.

We are proud and honored to exhibit so many of the Major Artists from this region for over 60 years; Morris Graves, Paul Horiuchi, Guy Anderson, Mark Tobey, William Cumming, Kathleen Adkison, James W. Washington, Jr., Margaret Tomkins, Kenneth Callahan, George Tsutakawa, Carl Morris, Hilda Morris, Richard Gilkey, Ambrose Patterson, Katherine Ace, Victoria Adams, Susan Bennerstrom, Lisa Gilley, Patty Haller, David Kroll, Jared Rue, Gerard Tsutakawa, & Malei Young.

As Seattle’s oldest fine art gallery, our future goals are to maintain the hard-earned reputations of the nationally renowned regional artists and to continue to exhibit and promote the immensely talented emerging artists from our region.

The friendship, encouragement, and patronage of our clients has been equally important to the success of our artists and gallery, for this, we are very thankful. We celebrate this Anniversary in honor of the founder of our gallery (Gordon Woodside 1927-2007) and the great Northwest artists that have gone before us.

– John Braseth, Director, Woodside/Braseth Gallery

mission

Vaunt Gallery is dedicated to discovering, curating, and showcasing some of the most compelling contemporary artists working today. With a sharp eye for innovation and a deep respect for craft, we travel the globe to bring extraordinary work to the Western United States and Canada.

We curate with layered discovery at the core—championing artists whose work sustains engagement beyond the initial encounter. We support artistic risk, cultivate collector insight, and build a community that values creativity as a force for connection, depth, and forward movement.

Vaunt Gallery is NOW Featuring DiStefano Wine to Bring Immersive Art & Wine Experience

Vaunt Gallery is debuting an immersive art and wine experience in Woodinville. DiStefano’s highly anticipated new wine release is unveiled inside Vaunt Gallery’s newly opened space, placing award-winning Washington wines within a curated exhibition of 25 internationally acclaimed contemporary artists.

---

Vaunt Gallery is connected to [The SOMM Hotel and Spa](https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=https-3A__thesomm.com_&d=DwMGaQ&c=euGZstcaTDllvimEN8b7jXrwqOf-v5A_CdpgnVfiiMM&r=XqhNWs5DwaMFz_ypEdSfFCEBlYjF1RuawHV-QqiOYxc&m=jFcHkxHG_MoyYODoZly1F2g7pRgVKlfgSykncR3tXxWFG9wDgzWqezuG5nGEXhTA&s=nGlvCmGVmBOO_RqY2vP5QwpHzFFhrm9S-FKC14zKABw&e=), a new retreat at the center of Harvest Woodinville.     

After a day of wine tasting, cycling, or exploring Harvest, visitors can unwind at The SOMM Hotel and Spa. With 164 thoughtfully designed rooms, The SOMM offers a welcoming place to stay in the heart of the Sammamish Valley. Guests can enjoy local flavors at Bin 47, sip craft brews at The Shed while taking in views of Mount Rainier, or gather around the fire in inviting shared spaces.

For those looking to relax and recharge, Vin de Spa offers a peaceful retreat, while the fitness center provides space to stay active. The SOMM also offers expansive event spaces for music performances, markets, celebrations, and gatherings of all kinds, with room for up to 600 seated guests or 1,000 guests for receptions.

With the Burke Gilman Trail nearby and more than 130 wineries, breweries, and distilleries throughout Woodinville, The SOMM and Vaunt Gallery serve as a welcoming base for discovering the region. This is truly a destination location for locals and a must-visit for wine enthusiasts.

# ART FOR COMMERCIAL AND RESIDENTIAL SPACES

## Translucent, Radiant Surfaces of Light and Pigment

Debra Van Tuinen creates large-scale paintings, prints, and encaustic works for corporate lobbies, hospitality interiors, and private residences— drawing on a 40+ year practice shown at the Seattle Art Fair, Art Basel Miami, and in embassy collections worldwide. Nordstrom, Hyatt, Hilton, Bank of America, and the Grand Rapids Art Museum hold her work, among others.

## WHAT THE CRITICS SEE

## Debra Van Tuinen's paintings possess radiance. They bask in the reflected light of a physical universe beyond the picture plane. This experiential, visionary world is the realm of painterly romanticism, as seen in the same non-linear sorts of compositions envisioned by Turner two centuries ago and Monet a hundred years later.

— Doug Meyer,  LA Critic

## “Everything you can imagine is real.”  Pablo Picasso

I spent much of my childhood up in trees where I felt hidden, safe and nurtured by their bounteous fruits. Often, I perched for hours at a time among the branches, reading, eating and resting.

               Recently, I drew twenty-two new drawings featuring people under or aloft in trees doing various activities: climbing a ladder, forming a ceramic plate, pressing tortilla dough, riding in a boat shaped like a banana, meditating, running, or dancing. I often wondered why I drew these scenes. Perhaps, as Picasso implied, they were real to me.

               My time in trees proved to be nurturing in both body and soul. While feeling safe, well fed and intellectually inspired by books, I grew physically and in spirit. Resting and day-dreaming also stimulated creativity, as symbolized by the ceramist with her plate, the tortilla maker or the dancers, activities I’ve enjoyed throughout my life. Meditating figures represent the deep repose I found in trees, spiritually connected to nature’s rhythms. I was fortunate to have been taught meditation when I was ten years old. I fell in love with quiet time spent observing my fleeting thoughts and letting them go, finding inner calm.

 The active figures I drew running or boating might well represent my physical and emotional development. I pursued running as a sport for decades. It’s also a symbol for enthusiastically pursuing a path, such as my art career. Meditating on a boat was an ancient Buddhist image, depicting the spiritual journey of a person traveling to “the other shore,” an enlightened realm, the Pure Land. When I meditate, I sometimes feel transported to a divine space.

                All of these visions originated from the healing I found in trees. Picasso was right; these recent twenty-two images sprang from my imagination and yet they proved to be real to me on an inner level.
